mission.beneficiary: Project owners who need to choose what to pursue, reject, or change before implementation and currently risk wasting labor through direction drift or elaborate but unproven planning.
mission.consequential_choice: sequence: pause feature expansion; execute and evaluate one complete equal-budget blinded case first, then continue to the remaining proof cases only if it yields credible comparative signal or a clear, repairable evaluation failure.
falsifiers: Blinded reviewers do not prefer the Palamedes output over the equal-budget one-shot baseline.
Any apparent preference disappears when information, token, compute, or review asymmetries are controlled.
The Palamedes output is more elaborate but does not change an attributable downstream choice.
The consequential choice produces no observable benefit, avoids no meaningful harm, and retires no owner labor.
A simpler static process or ordinary planner produces an equally strong mission from the same packet.
The experiment cannot separate mission quality from planning, implementation, environmental, or measurement effects well enough to support learning.
mission.interpretation: The project’s binding uncertainty is comparative decision value, not missing architecture, schemas, retrieval coverage, or agent features. Further feature expansion would increase ceremony before establishing that Palamedes improves upstream judgment.
mission.mission: Run the smallest preregistered, equal-budget, blinded baseline-versus-Palamedes experiment that yields an attributable consequential mission choice and records its downstream outcome.
mission.next_probe: Complete the frozen insight-rag paired pilot by generating the one-shot baseline and bounded Palamedes treatment under declared budgets, blind their origins, obtain independent reviews against preregistered criteria, and trace whether the selected mission changes a real action and owner workload.
non_goals: Expanding the analyzer, corpus, retrieval system, schemas, or reference adapters.
Adding queues, schedulers, shell execution, manager hierarchies, plugins, or unbounded autonomy.
Claiming general superiority, creativity, originality, or startup success from one case.
Treating test counts, schema validity, reasoning-cycle volume, indexed records, or rejection of a bad packet as evidence of better decisions.
Polishing philosophical ontology or view-transition lineage unless required to execute or interpret the comparison.
mission.rationale: This directly tests the product hypothesis with existing proof machinery while minimizing cost and self-serving expansion. A single rigorously completed case cannot establish broad superiority, but it can validate the evaluation loop, produce the first comparative evidence, and determine whether completing the three-project proof program is warranted.
mission.situation: Palamedes has a stable, heavily tested planning kernel and has shown that its safety protocol can reject a bad retrieval treatment, but it has not yet shown that its pre-planning process produces better decisions than a one-shot baseline under equal information and budget.
mission.success_signal: From the same frozen information packet and transparently reported compute budgets, blinded reviewers prefer the Palamedes mission contract over the one-shot baseline, and the preferred contract causes a documented stop, pivot, positioning, or sequencing choice whose downstream consequence and owner labor effect can be observed.
